🎯 The 12 Cranial Nerves

Mnemonic: “Oh Oh Oh To Touch And Feel Very Good Velvet, Ah Heaven.” Type key: S = sensory, M = motor, B = both.

#NameTypeCore function
IOlfactorySSmell
IIOpticSVision
IIIOculomotorMMost eye movements, pupil constriction, eyelid opening
IVTrochlearMSuperior oblique — moves eye down & in
VTrigeminalBFace sensation; muscles of mastication
VIAbducensMLateral rectus — abducts the eye
VIIFacialBFacial expression; taste, anterior ⅔ of tongue
VIIIVestibulocochlearSHearing and balance
IXGlossopharyngealBTaste, posterior ⅓ tongue; swallowing; gag afferent
XVagusBSwallowing, voice, parasympathetics to thorax & abdomen; gag efferent
XIAccessoryMSternocleidomastoid & trapezius — head turn, shoulder shrug
XIIHypoglossalMTongue movement — tongue deviates toward the lesion

🔬 Core Diagrams

The Neuron

Dendrites receive signals → soma (cell body) holds the nucleus → the axon hillock decides whether to fire → the signal travels the myelinated axon (myelin speeds conduction; nodes of Ranvier allow saltatory conduction) → axon terminals release neurotransmitter. Signals flow one way: dendrite → soma → axon → terminal.

The Chemical Synapse — 6 Steps

  1. Action potential arrives at the terminal.
  2. Voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels open; Ca²⁺ flows in.
  3. Ca²⁺ triggers synaptic vesicles to fuse and release neurotransmitter.
  4. Transmitter crosses the synaptic cleft and binds receptors on the postsynaptic cell.
  5. Postsynaptic channels open → EPSP (excitatory) or IPSP (inhibitory).
  6. Signal ends by reuptake, enzymatic breakdown (e.g., acetylcholinesterase for ACh), or diffusion.

Two Pathways You Must Never Mix Up

Dorsal column–medial lemniscus: fine touch, vibration, conscious proprioception. Crosses in the medulla (internal arcuate fibers). Lesion below the medulla → same-side loss.

Spinothalamic (anterolateral): pain and temperature. Crosses in the spinal cord itself, in the anterior white commissure, ~1–2 levels above entry. Lesion → opposite-side loss starting a couple of levels below the lesion.

Spinal Cord — Key Levels

31 spinal nerve pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal. The cord itself ends at the conus medullaris (~L1–L2 in adults); below that runs the cauda equina — which is why lumbar puncture is done at L3–L4 or L4–L5. Cervical nerves C1–C7 exit above their vertebra; C8 and all below exit below.

Find them by their 🔎 markers on the street, at the store, or in the Menu under Explore the Castle.
  17. There is music in this castle. The 🎵 Music Room (in the ☰ Menu, under Explore the Castle and under Sound & Music) holds songs your son Domenick composed for you — press play and listen while you study or rest. If a player ever won't load, the room's Castle Tones play gentle music the game makes itself, right on your device.

🎭 The Teachers' Lounge

Nineteen teachers with real faces wander Neurology Street, Sandra — each one teaches one subject, and only that subject, and each one has a sense of humor. And then there's Uncle Knickknack — he's in here too, and he's the exception to every rule: he wanders where he pleases and breaks any neurology down plain, the apothecary way. Walk up to them outside, or say hello right here. Ask a question, get your answer… and then wait for it. They can't resist one little joke afterwards — a touch of smart sarcasm, all in good fun, to keep you comfortable.

🧍🏿‍♂️

The Dude — at the Corner Store

Not a professor. The same dude who is always posted up outside the liquor store on your block.

He teaches nothing from a book — he teaches what he sees: the neurology and psychology of the people on the block, in street clothes. Find him at the store, or right here.

🏠 Home — Sandra's House

Your house on the block, Sandra — same as real life. This is where the day starts: you come out the front door, your truck is parked at the curb, and the whole street is yours. Rest here a minute, check your notes, name your test — then head out: walk the block, drive to the store, or step into the castle and study.

🍲 THE CROCK POT — LOW AND SLOW, LIKE ALWAYS

Your crock pot sits right here on the counter, same as home.

🏪 The Corner Store & Liquor Store

Every block in LA has one, and this is yours, Sandra — the corner store you drive your truck to. Cold drinks, snacks, the lottery board, the bell over the door… and posted up outside, right where he always is: the same dude. He is part of this block the way the palm trees are. Say hello — he's got street observations of his own, and more neurology hides in this store than in half the textbooks.

🧍🏿‍♂️ THE DUDE — OUTSIDE THE STORE, SAME AS ALWAYS

“Well, look who pulled up. Doctor Sandra. I been on this corner so long, the corner got seniority off ME. You want to know what I know? I know PEOPLE. I watch 'em all day — and half of what I watch is that neurology of yours, just wearing street clothes. Come on, let me show you what I see.”

🧾 THE CLERK — BEHIND THE COUNTER

“Doctor Sandra. Your usual's already in my head — I don't forget a face, and I sure don't forget yours. You here for the chicken, or you stocking up for a study run? Take my word: the Study Fuel shelf by the register — that's the college shelf. Water, trail mix, coffee. Brains run on that stuff, and yours is running toward a PhD. Everything on that shelf earns its place in your Bag.”

🛒 Groceries — the real reason for the trip

This is your routine, Sandra: drive down to the corner store, pick up something good, take it home, and let the crock pot do the rest. Whatever you grab here goes straight into your Bag — the chicken is for home, and the rest keeps Uncle working when a battle drags.

🧠 Study Fuel — keep your mind right, Doctor

The college shelf, right by the register — what a student grabs to keep her mindset straight through a long study run. Nothing here is decoration: every single one works for you in a battle, and every battle won is the degree getting closer. Stock up before you fight.

🔎 Scenes to observe in and around this store

🔎 Street Observations

Neurology doesn't only live in the castle, Sandra — it walks around on your block all day. Every scene here is something a person can really see on a street in Los Angeles: what Sandra noticed, what's happening in the brain, and what's happening in the people — the psychology of the world around you. Read the scene, then answer its question: +15 XP for every observation you complete.

📝 Correct This — Agamos Will Fix It

Correcting:

Your studies and your intelligence come first, Sandra. Type what should be fixed, in your own words. Agamos will take your correction, fix it in the system, and tag it: Corrected by Sandra Annette Hall.
